outline.title: Proctor
outline.summary: Your agent said the tests pass. Proctor checks. Developer guide and product overview for v0.1.0.

outline.title: The missing question in agent-assisted development
outline.summary: Explain how agent reports, diff review, and CI can miss filtered tests, weakened assertions, deleted tests, or bypassed hooks.

outline.title: Proctor turns agent claims into reviewable evidence
outline.summary: Introduce the wrapper, deterministic ledger, claim adjudication, and portable Work Receipt.

outline.title: One local-first pipeline, four useful outputs
outline.summary: Show the run, analyze, receipt, and decide pipeline and its local-first privacy model.

outline.title: The 30-second developer workflow
outline.summary: Demonstrate the three-command workflow and the resulting receipt and gate behavior.

outline.title: The CLI is designed for agent handoffs
outline.summary: Summarize run, verify, gate, inspect, and badge with their developer outcomes and package naming note.

outline.title: A Work Receipt is the durable handoff artifact
outline.summary: Explain the ledger, claims, findings, integrity, and optional signature sections of a receipt.

outline.title: Green-wash detectors create a shared vocabulary
outline.summary: Show representative GW detectors, evidence anchors, maturity, and conservative evidence policy.

outline.title: From local run to pull-request gate
outline.summary: Show the GitHub Action configuration and what it does with receipts, gates, badges, and comments.

outline.title: Adopt Proctor without changing your agent
outline.summary: Give a low-friction adoption path, privacy controls, strict-mode progression, and development extensibility.

outline.title: Evidence first, automation second
outline.summary: State anti-goals, current limitations, and roadmap items for developers.

outline.title: Start auditing the next agent run
outline.summary: Close with installation, execution, verification, and links to GitHub, npm, taxonomy, and README.
